title: John Floyd
summary: Surveyor John Floyd stockaded Floyd’s Station near today’s St. Matthews in 1779 and became one of Kentucky’s first judges before his death in 1783.
bodyMarkdown:
[John Floyd](https://grokipedia.com/page/john_floyd_%28pioneer%29) was a surveyor, militia officer and early judge who helped lay out Louisville. He was born in 1750 in Amherst County, Virginia. As a young man he lived in the home of William Preston, the surveyor for Virginia's vast Fincastle County, and became his deputy surveyor.

## The 1774 survey

In 1774 Preston chose Floyd to lead a party of surveyors toward the Falls of the Ohio. While there, Floyd claimed a 2,000-acre site for himself in what is now St. Matthews. Lord Dunmore's War with the Shawnee was then breaking out, and Native warriors attacked the group, killing two surveyors. Floyd made his way back to Virginia in 16 days and arrived half a day late for the Battle of Point Pleasant.

## Boonesborough and the Atlantic

Floyd returned in 1775 and served as a delegate to the Transylvania meeting at Boonesborough, the earliest attempt at government west of the Alleghenies. In July 1776 he helped rescue Jemima Boone and two other girls from a party of four Shawnee and one Cherokee.

Later that year he joined a privateering venture at sea. The British captured him and held him at Forton Prison in England. He escaped to Paris in 1777, where American envoys lent him money to get home. There he bought wedding clothes and a scarlet coat.

## Floyd's Station

Floyd married Jane Buchanan in 1778 and came back to the Falls in 1779. He settled his 2,000 acres near Beargrass Creek, where ten more families joined him and a stockade was added. The place became known as Floyd's Station.

In 1780 the Virginia General Assembly named Floyd one of seven trustees of Louisville. In 1781 he became county lieutenant of Jefferson County, in charge of its defense. That September, the day after the [Long Run massacre](https://grokipedia.com/page/long_run_massacre), he led 27 men to bury the dead and was ambushed. Seventeen of his men were killed, and the fight became known as Floyd's Defeat. A Wyandot chief also died in that clash.

Floyd later took part in the [Battle of Blue Licks](/stories/battle-of-blue-licks/) and in [George Rogers Clark](/stories/george-rogers-clark/)'s 1782 raid on Shawnee towns along the Great Miami River.

## Death on the road

In 1783 Virginia organized a court for Kentucky and named Floyd one of its first two judges. On April 8, while riding toward [Bullitt's Lick](/stories/bullitts-lick-kentuckys-first-industry/) in his scarlet coat from Paris, he was shot by Native attackers. He died on April 10. Born in 1750, he was about 32 or 33.

## Kentucky today

Floyd County, Floyds Fork and Floyd Street in Louisville are all named for him. Floyd's Station Springhouse still stands, and Floyd is buried at Breckinridge Cemetery near the station site. His Beargrass neighbor [William Christian](/stories/william-christian-of-beargrass/) also has a story on this site.
